title: Desk surface protocol v0: lifecycle
description: A surface's life: create, resize, show and hide, sleep and wake, destroy, from the compositor; ready, died and its title, from the surface. See lifecycle.md.

SurfaceOwner.description: Whose content the surface draws: a plugin id, or desk for the desk's own system surfaces (palette, Eris, bars, settings).

SurfaceView.description: Which of the owner's surfaces to draw: the id of a surfaces entry of its plugin.json.

SurfaceCreate.description: Make a surface and start drawing it. It starts shown unless hidden is true; it answers ready once it takes input, and attaches its first frame when it has one.

hidden.description: Start hidden: load, but paint nothing until show. Default false.

SurfaceResize.description: Lay out at a new logical size or scale (a window resized, or moved to another display). The surface's next frames come at the new pixel size; until one does, the compositor draws the last frame anchored at the top left.

SurfaceShow.description: The surface is on screen again: paint at the pace the compositor last set.

SurfaceHide.description: The surface is off screen (WasHidden): stop painting, keep running and keep its state. The compositor keeps its last frame.

SurfaceSleep.description: The surface left the live budget: save its state, stop painting, and let its process exit. That exit is not a death. The compositor shows its last frame, greyed.

SurfaceWake.description: Start a sleeping or dead surface again at this size: a new process if it had none, its saved state restored, then ready and a frame.

SurfaceDestroy.description: The surface is closed for good: free everything. No message about it follows from either side.

SurfaceReady.description: The surface is loaded and takes input. Once after create and once after each wake; frames may come before it.

SurfaceDeathReason.description: Why a surface's process ended without being asked to: it crashed, something killed it, it ran out of memory, it could not start, or it exited by itself.

SurfaceDied.description: The surface's process ended while it was not asleep. Its host sends this (the dead process cannot): the web host from the engine's signal, the native host when the process exits. The compositor shows a placeholder; wake starts it again.

exitCode.description: The process's exit code or signal number, when the host knows it.

SurfaceTitle.description: The surface's title changed (a page's document.title): the compositor shows it in the window's chrome and its switchers.
